card.statement:
[<<cite:MR97k:17014>>] A basis for $U_q$ is the set of monomials of the form

$$
x^-a^-K^\alpha D^{\beta}\gamma^{\mu/2}a^+x^+
$$

where

\begin{align*}
x^\pm&=x^\pm(m_1)^{n_1}\cdots x^\pm(m_k)^{n_k},
\quad\quad m_i<m_{i+1},\quad m_i\in\mathbb Z,  \\
a^\pm&=a(r_1)^{s_1}\cdots a(r_l)^{s_l},
\quad\quad r_i<r_{i+1},\quad \pm r_i\in\mathbb N^*,
\end{align*}

and $\alpha,\beta,\mu\in\mathbb Z,\, n_i,s_i\in\mathbb N$. In particular, $U_q \cong U_q^-(S) \otimes U_q^0(S) \otimes U_q^+(S)$.
card.label: Theorem 4

paper.title: Imaginary Verma modules and Kashiwara algebras for $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}(2)})$
paper.abstract: We consider imaginary Verma modules for quantum affine algebra $U_q(\hat{\mathfrak{sl}(2)})$ and construct Kashiwara type operators and the Kashiwara algebra $\mathcal K_q$. We show that a certain quotient $\mathcal N_q^-$ of $U_q(\hat{\mathfrak{sl}(2)})$ is a simple $\mathcal K_q$-module.
